selections.comment: A good quality renewal of this Grade 3 contest. Successful 12 months ago, WINTER FOG is back to defend his crown. Despite his advancing years, the 11-year-old clearly retains plenty of enthusiasm for the game, with his form at Cheltenham and Punchestown reading very well in the context of this race. Willie Mullins trains the selection and also saddles Gaucher and Batman Girac, with both capable of making an impact. The only four-year-old in the line-up, Puturhandstogether is an intriguing contender. An easy winner of the Fred Winter at Cheltenham in March, he since finished third in Grade 1 company at Aintree. The Andy Slattery-trained pair of Sunchart and Smooth Tom both warrant respect, while it will be interesting to see how Feud fares on his return from a lengthy absence.

Amboyna is capable of making an impact if putting her best foot forward, with course winner Eaglewood and Punchestown third Coded Welder others for the shortlist.

Gordon Elliott is represented by Themanintheboots, Irina's Path and Penny Express, with Jack Kennedy set to partner the former, who filled the runner-up spot on recent starts at Listowel and Downpatrick respectively.

selections.comment: DYSART ENOS has strong claims to make a winning Flat debut. New to this surface but well seasoned over jumps and in bumpers, winning six races of 10 races under rules, inclding a Grade 2 win in a bumper at Aintree she has shown tremendous ability and there's no reason that can't be translated to the Flat. She should prove tough to beat. Mission Possible looks the biggest danger after a decent introduction when beaten eight lengths after being green and leaving a lot to do. She should come on plenty for that exeperience and can give the selction most to do. Ritaan is also a threat having improved on a fair debut when second at Ripon last time and can take another step forward here to challenge for honours. The newcomer Debradini, a valuable breeze-up purchase, is interesting and looks likely to go well on her debut and could get in the mix along with Glint Of Light, who should appreciate the drop back in trip and wouldn't need too much improvement to get involved in the finish

He's not shown his best in handicap company yet but remains very promsing after just six runs and could go close

It won't take much of a step forward on those recent efforts to land top prize here. Tyger Bay could go well and is feared most having found his level again, and with conditions to suit and an ease in grade he can run the selection very close. There could be a bit more to come from the admirably reliable Papabella and she can be trusted to give best again having gone close over course and distance in April but better is also expected from General Assembly back on the AW and he could out-run his odds to lay down a serious challenge and reach the frame

He is still improving and gets the verdict ahead of 2022 C&D Graded winner Jesse Evans who found the ground too quick at Royal Ascot last time but proved he retained his ability over hurdles previously. Fred Winter winner Puturhandstogether is arguably open to the most improvement in the field and isn't dismissed either in a strong race for the grade.
